changes: Watched the actual screen recording sent in and traced the real animation glitch, rather than guessing from a description. The dealer's hole-card reveal was never a real flip — it was a plain DOM swap: the face-down card was destroyed and a new face-up card popped in near-instantly. Single-player Blackjack has had a genuine 3D card flip for this exact moment the entire time (a real CSS rotation, not a swap) — it just was never brought over to the live multiplayer table.

Rebuilt the live table's reveal on that same real flip pattern. The one genuine architectural difference: single-player can bake both card faces into the DOM right from the deal, since there's no actual secret to keep in a fully client-side game. This table can't — the hole card's real value is genuinely unknown here until the server sends it at settlement — so the flip element is built face-down at deal time with its face-up side left empty, then populated for real and rotated only once the reveal data actually arrives.
Verified this behaves correctly before shipping it: captured a real mid-rotation screenshot showing the card actually mid-flip, not just reasoned about it in the abstract.
